subject: ela
skillName: Identify main topic and key details

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: Dolphins are smart ocean mammals. They breathe air through a blowhole on the top of their heads.

Paragraph 2: Dolphins live in groups called pods. They play together, hunt fish together, and protect each other from sharks. Dolphins use clicks and whistles to communicate with their pod members.

What is the main topic of this article?

steps: Both paragraphs are about dolphins. The main topic is dolphins.
solution.answer: The main topic of this article is dolphins.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: Plants need four things to grow: sunlight, water, soil, and air.

Paragraph 2: Roots are the part of a plant that soaks up water and nutrients from the soil. They also anchor the plant so it does not fall over. Some plants, like carrots and radishes, store food in their roots.

What is the focus of paragraph 2?

steps: Paragraph 2 is only about roots — what they do and how some plants use them.
Focus: the role of roots in plants.
solution.answer: The focus of paragraph 2 is roots and what they do for plants.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: Ancient Rome was one of the most powerful civilizations in history. At its peak, it ruled most of Europe, North Africa, and parts of the Middle East.

Paragraph 2: Roman engineers built an amazing network of roads across the empire. The roads were straight, paved with stone, and well-drained. They allowed soldiers and trade goods to move quickly. Many Roman roads are still visible today.

What is the focus of paragraph 2?

steps: Paragraph 2 is about Roman roads — how they were built and why they were important.
Focus: Roman roads and their importance to the empire.
solution.answer: The focus of paragraph 2 is the roads that Roman engineers built and how they helped the empire.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: Hibernation is a deep sleep that some animals enter during winter. While hibernating, an animal's body temperature drops and its heartbeat slows way down.

Paragraph 2: Not all animals that seem to hibernate actually do. Bears enter a lighter sleep called torpor. During torpor, bears can wake up more easily than true hibernators. True hibernators, like groundhogs and hedgehogs, are almost impossible to wake because their body processes slow down so much.

What is the main topic? What does paragraph 2 add to the topic?

steps: Main topic: hibernation and winter sleep in animals.
Paragraph 2 adds an important distinction: not all winter sleep is true hibernation. Bears sleep in torpor, which is lighter than true hibernation.
solution.answer: The main topic is animal hibernation. Paragraph 2 adds the important point that not all winter sleep is true hibernation — bears enter a lighter state called torpor, unlike true hibernators like groundhogs.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: The Amazon River in South America is one of the longest rivers in the world. It carries more water than any other river on Earth.

Paragraph 2: The Amazon River Basin is home to the largest rainforest on Earth. Millions of plant and animal species live in this vast forest. The Amazon River and its rainforest together play a key role in regulating Earth's climate by absorbing carbon dioxide.

What is the main topic? What is the focus of paragraph 2?

steps: Main topic: the Amazon River.
Paragraph 2 focuses on the Amazon River Basin — the rainforest that surrounds the river — and its role in Earth's climate.
solution.answer: The main topic is the Amazon River. The focus of paragraph 2 is the Amazon River Basin rainforest and its role in regulating Earth's climate.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: The human skeleton is made up of more than 200 bones. Bones give the body its shape and protect organs like the heart and lungs.

Paragraph 2: Bones are not dead — they are living tissue that grows and changes. Red blood cells are made inside the soft center of bones, called bone marrow. If a bone breaks, special cells called osteoblasts build new bone tissue to repair it.

What does paragraph 2 explain that might surprise a reader who only read paragraph 1?

steps: Paragraph 1 describes the skeleton as a structural support.
Paragraph 2 reveals that bones are living and can grow, make blood cells, and repair themselves.
This might surprise readers who think bones are just hard and lifeless.
solution.answer: Paragraph 2 might surprise readers by revealing that bones are living tissue — they make red blood cells in bone marrow and can repair themselves when broken.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: The California Gold Rush began in 1848 when gold was discovered at Sutter's Mill. News spread quickly, and within a year, about 80,000 people rushed to California hoping to strike it rich.

Paragraph 2: Most gold rush miners did not become wealthy. The gold became harder to find, and the cost of supplies was very high. However, the rush transformed California. Towns grew into cities, roads and ports were built, and California's population grew so fast it became a state in 1850.

What is the main topic of this article? Summarize what each paragraph is mostly about and explain how the two paragraphs together give a complete picture of the Gold Rush.

steps: Main topic: the California Gold Rush.
Paragraph 1 focuses on how the Gold Rush started and how many people came.
Paragraph 2 focuses on what actually happened — few got rich, but California was transformed.
Together, paragraph 1 tells us the beginning and excitement of the Gold Rush, and paragraph 2 tells us the results, completing the picture.
solution.answer: The main topic is the California Gold Rush. Paragraph 1 covers how the rush started and attracted 80,000 people. Paragraph 2 covers the outcomes — few miners got rich, but California grew rapidly and became a state. Together, the paragraphs give a complete picture: the exciting start and the lasting consequences.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Paragraph 1: Wind energy is a clean, renewable source of power. Wind turbines use spinning blades to capture the energy in moving air and convert it into electricity.

Paragraph 2: Wind energy has both advantages and limitations. On the positive side, it produces no pollution and the wind is free. On the negative side, wind turbines only work when the wind blows, and they need to be built in windy areas. Some people also object to the noise and appearance of large turbines near their homes.

What is the main topic? What approach does paragraph 2 take that paragraph 1 does not? Why is this approach important for understanding wind energy fully?

steps: Main topic: wind energy.
Paragraph 1 introduces wind energy positively.
Paragraph 2 takes a balanced approach — it presents both advantages and limitations.
This balanced approach is important because it gives the reader a complete, honest picture rather than just one side.
solution.answer: The main topic is wind energy. Paragraph 2 takes a balanced approach by presenting both advantages and limitations, which paragraph 1 does not do. This is important because it gives readers a full, honest understanding of wind energy rather than a one-sided view.
